subject: SOC2, EU residency & export-control checks — follow-up and action plan

Subject: SOC2, EU residency & export-control checks — follow-up and action plan

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Lina — nice to meet you and the StorApp team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Call highlights (30m):
- Your priority: confirm SOC 2 coverage + ability to keep inference data in EU regions for EU customers.
- Compliance concerns: GDPR & HIPAA applicability for a subset of PII/PHI; vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) needed for procurement.
- Export-control checks: you flagged potential OFAC/ITAR questions for customers operating in regulated industries.

Requested items from StorApp (action: Lina / Legal):
1) Start the vendor security questionnaire — please send your latest completed VSQ or the form you prefer us to fill.
2) Confirm the minimum SOC 2 artifact you require (Type II report within last 12 months?).
3) Any specific export-control language or ITAR/OFAC redlines to surface up-front.

What we’ll provide (action: Redwood):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report + evidence index (attached).
- Short note on EU region availability and data residency options (hosted routing vs Private/VPC).
- Preliminary answers to high-level export controls / sanctions posture; legal to follow if needed.

Attachments: redwood-region-capabilities.pdf (quick summary of EU region options).

Proposed timeline:
- Lina: send VSQ and SOC2 artifact request by EOD Wed (24 Jun).
- Redwood: turn-around for VSQ answers and SOC2 redacted copy within 48 hours of receiving the form.

If that looks right I’ll loop in our security lead (Rishi) and legal (Priyom) to handle technical and contractual questions.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.example | +1 415-555-0192

Thanks, Monica — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- VSQ: attaching our standard vendor questionnaire (StorApp_Vendor_Q_2026.docx). Please complete and return; procurement requires it for all new vendors.
- SOC2: we require a SOC2 Type II report covering security within the last 12 months (redacted copies are acceptable).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, Lina Gomes <lina.gomes@storapp.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2, EU residency & export-control checks — follow-up and action plan

Hi Lina / Monica — looping in technical and security details below. Short version: we can support your asks but there are a few important distinctions between deployment modes.

1) SOC 2
- We maintain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Redwood hosted platform (security). Redacted report (PDF) is attached; full bridge call available under NDA.
- Evidence index available on request; Priyom can coordinate any contract-level requests.

2) Data residency & regional processing
- Hosted API: We operate EU regions (Amsterdam and Frankfurt). For hosted customers we can ensure inference request processing and at-rest storage for embeddings are restricted to an EU region (configured per-customer).
- Control plane metadata: metadata used for routing/healthing is stored in the control plane; for standard hosted customers control plane services may be in our control plane region set. If StorApp requires strict physical separation (no control-plane cross-border metadata), Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem deployment is the recommended option.
- Private/VPC: full-data residency (including control-plane options) is available with our Private deployment package; we can provide a design doc and runbook.

3) Cross-border transfers & GDPR
- We support EU-only data processing for customer inference payloads and persisted embeddings. We will provide a DPA addendum clarifying subprocessors and transfer mechanisms (SCCs or adequacy path if applicable).

4) Export controls (OFAC/ITAR)
- OFAC / sanctions: Redwood enforces sanctions screening for account onboarding and for API keys associated with flagged entities. We cannot process data for sanctioned parties. We will provide our sanctions policy excerpt.
- ITAR: Redwood’s standard hosted offering is not pre-cleared for ITAR-controlled technical data. Processing ITAR material requires an approved Private deployment with vetted hosting and contractual controls (and potentially export licensing). If StorApp expects ITAR workloads, please indicate scope so we can engage our legal/ops team.

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-report-redacted.pdf, redwood-data-residency-faq.pdf

Let me know if you want a short 30-min technical call to walk through the Private deployment design and what a DPA with SCCs would look like.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.example

Attachment: redwood-soc2-report-redacted.pdf (redacted PDF)
Attachment: redwood-data-residency-faq.pdf (2 page FAQ)

Thanks, Rishi — that helps a lot. A few quick clarifications from legal: 
- Redacted SOC2 PDF looks fine for initial review.
- StorApp prefers to keep inference processing + persisted embeddings in EU-only infrastructure; control-plane metadata is a negotiable item but needs to be minimized for our EU customers.
- We do not currently have ITAR data to process, but we may work with defense-adjacent customers later this year; we’ll flag those earlier if/when they arise.

Procurement timeline: we’ll complete and return your VSQ by Fri (26 Jun) and aim to review Redwood’s redacted SOC2 + VSQ responses by 30 Jun. If all looks good, procurement will prepare the drafting team for DPA/SCCs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Lina
